evidence: SOURCE sentence replaced: 'The useful question is whether this way of responding helps you become clearer, steadier, and less hooked.' DRAFT: 'Is this way of responding helping you to be clearer and steadier and less hooked?' Checked piece by piece: the test is the same (does this way of responding help you); the three outcomes are his three in his order (clearer, steadier, less hooked); 'this way of responding' is his phrase, and the_change says it stands in for Emulate's 'it', which is what the draft shows; the reader is still the one helped. No claim, fact, number or person is added. Shifts weighed: (1) the declarative 'The useful question is whether' became a direct question, so 'useful' and the assertion that this is the question to ask are no longer in the sentence itself; the section carries them (heading 'A response check, not a verdict about what it is'; the sentence before, 'You don't have to find out if it's a guard immediately', is the redirect away from the verdict), so the question reads as the check the heading promises and the reader does what his line asked of them; (2) 'helps ... become' turned into 'helping ... to be' (general to in-the-moment, become to be), which asks the same thing at the moment of a response check; (3) the commas became 'and ... and' (see O14). None of these changes what the reader is asked to judge. CONTEXT holds the draft once, as the last sentence of the section; 'this way of responding' points at the responses in the paragraphs before it (warm or arm's length, the Nurturer, stopping) under the heading 'A response check', and his own phrase had the same reach after 'Neither response', so C02 is fine. Tell rows: none PRESENT. T02 considered at section scale: the section is a procedure by genre, the draft adds no step and keeps the job of the sentence it replaces, so any cadence there is not this change's. T20, T28 and T29 considered because the question is the last sentence of its paragraph and of its section (the ledger's evidence that it is not the end of its section is wrong); not present: it is the check the heading promises rather than a lesson, reassurance or summary, it is plain and fifteen words long rather than a short polished closer, and without it the paragraph would end on two reassurances and no instruction, so it is a new consideration and not a restatement. T24 not present (nothing answers the question). T26 considered: 'helps' recurs from the paragraph that says 'Find out if it helps to be warm...', but the question supplies the criteria that paragraph lacks. T12: the triad is his published three, not new. T15: not present, the draft returns his phrase rather than swapping to a less likely one. All other rows (T01, T03 to T11, T13, T14, T16 to T19, T21 to T23, T25, T27, C01, C03, C04) ABSENT. Linter: D9 accepted (one sentence, forced order, T13 and T09 absent); the writer's reason cites Emulate asides ('if I can put it that way', 'of course', 'just', '!') that this draft does not contain, so I accepted it on the context, not that reason. E36/E41 accepted: 1 'you' in 15 words (6.7), about the same as the sentence it replaces (1 in 17, 5.9). O14 accepted, with the most weight of the three: the list is exactly the shape the flag names (his comma list 'clearer, steadier, and less hooked' turned into 'clearer and steadier and less hooked'), but it is one three-item question that a reader would say or think aloud, nothing in meaning moves, and the same section already speaks this way ('sadness or fear or like you're trying to protect something').
